regime_context: The detector shows a coordinated precious-metals leadership in Canada: Gold Miners (rank 1) and Silver & Royalties (rank 2) are both trend-tagged with high breadth and durability, while the broad eligible set (69% of themes) confirms a wide rotation rather than a one-narrative squeeze. The validated edge here is the absolute-trend gate (gate_helps true) — risk control, not return forecasting — and the backtests confirm momentum rank is ~no alpha, so any lean is a durability/trend-discipline judgement, not a prediction.
emerging_watch: Watching whether Silver & Royalties closes the rotation margin to Gold Miners (score gap below ~0.2) on sustained breadth — a confirmed handoff would shift the precious-metals read toward silver leadership before the check-by date; a widening margin retires the watch.

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners is the confirmed leader with the strongest durability_bar (0.79) and hurst_tag 'trend', plus the highest breadth (0.867) among top names — the trend-gate leg supports staying power, not a return forecast. The eligible + trend + broad-breadth combination is the one checkable read allowed by the discipline: stay with the confirmed trend until it breaks, not because it might outperform, but because it is the cleanest trend-health picture.
evidence: rotation.leader is ca_gold with margin 0.4 over challenger
theses.dissent: Gold miners are momentum-flagged with no alpha edge (rank-IC ~0), and the headline theme typically marks attention rather than forward return; a crowded-adjacent precious metals complex could stall on a risk-on macro rotation away from defensives.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO closes below its 20-day low before the check-by date

theses.subject: Silver & Royalties
theses.thesis: Silver & Royalties is the nearest challenger (score 1.712) with perfect breadth (1.0) and high durability_bar (0.76), eligible and uncrowded — a secondary trend-health confirmation of the same precious-metals leadership, differentiated only by slightly lower durability and a 'mixed' hurst tag (less clean than Gold). The rotation margin (0.4) shows no confirmed handoff, so this is a companion trend lean, not a prediction.
theses.dissent: Silver is more volatile and less pure a trend than gold; the 'mixed' hurst tag means its trend health is less reliable, and a precious-metals shake-out could hit silver beta harder than gold.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO lags Gold Miners by 4% on a 20-day relative basis

theses.subject: Base Metals & Copper
theses.thesis: Base Metals & Copper is eligible with a decent score (1.375) but is the only top-3 name flagged crowded (crowding_z 1.12) with a 'mixed' hurst tag — the crowding leg is a SIZE-DOWN caution only, never a fade, and combined with lower durability (0.73) it argues for stepping aside rather than adding trend risk here.
theses.dissent: Copper could benefit from a broad industrial reflation bid; avoiding it may miss a strong cyclical continuation, and crowding flags have no basket-level forward edge (only per-name crash texture).

falsifier.text: XBM.TO breaks to a new 60-day high while not overextended

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
